_comment:
English copy for the Ihsaanly website. Every other language is src/i18n/messages/.json with the same shape; any key it leaves out falls back to English and is listed by `bun run build:site`. Keys named _comment or ending in _comment are notes for translators and are never shown. Values may contain only , , and
. Words in braces such as {privacy} are filled in by the build or the page: keep them exactly as written, and move them wherever the sentence needs them. Keep the product name Ihsaanly, the company name Mohd Inc. and the store names App Store and Google Play in Latin letters. Call the Chrome Web Store by its official name in your language.

day.title: You mark the prayer. The sunnah appears.
day.intro: Tap Dhuhr when you have prayed it, and the dhikr that follows is waiting. The app shows the part of the day you are in, not a clock time, so it never competes with your mosque’s timetable.
day.maghribFirst: The day begins at Maghrib, so the app’s day does too.

timeline._comment: The day as a timeline, one row per prayer. The prayer names are usually kept as they are.
timeline.ishaWhat: Two rak’ah after, then Witr. Before you sleep, Ayat al-Kursi, the Quls and the dua for sleeping.
timeline.fajrWhat: The dua on waking, and two rak’ah before the prayer.
timeline.sunriseWhat: The morning adhkar, and Duha once the sun is up.
timeline.dhuhrWhat: Two or four rak’ah before, and two after.
timeline.asrWhat: The evening adhkar, until Maghrib comes round again.

day.outro: After every prayer, the tasbih and Ayat al-Kursi. For the moments no clock can find, such as leaving home, setting off or going up a flight of stairs, the duas are a tap away on a home screen widget.

source.title: Every item shows its source
source.intro: Each act shows where it comes from: the verse, or the hadith collection with its reference and grading, and who graded it where the collection does not carry its own. Where scholars differ, the app says so rather than choosing for you.
source.plain: Every item also explains, in plain words, why it matters and how to do it.

specimen._comment: A sample dua card. The Arabic stays Arabic; the dua titles and meanings come from the app's own translated content. Only the buttons and the source lines are here.
specimen.leavingTitle_comment: Used only if the app's content has no title in this language.
specimen.ridingGrading: Sunan Abi Dawud 2602, graded sahih by al-Albani.

coming.title: Know what is coming
coming.fasting: Fasting days appear in advance: Mondays and Thursdays, the White Days, Ashura, Arafah and the six of Shawwal. They are marked “expected”, because they are calculated rather than sighted.
coming.shift: If your community’s Hijri date differs, shift it by up to two days and everything follows.

calm.title: Calm by design
calm.reminders: Two or three reminders a day, not fifteen, and nothing during quiet hours. Dismiss anything without explaining yourself. Learn a dua and mark it as known, and the app stops reminding you about it.
calm.owed: Prayers and fasts you owe are kept as a simple count to make up, never a list of dates. You will not find:
calm.neverStreaks: Streaks, scores or leaderboards on acts of worship
calm.neverFailed: A notification telling you that you failed
calm.neverPaywall: A paywall on any religious content

inside.adhkar: Morning and evening adhkar, and the tasbih and Ayat al-Kursi after prayer
inside.prayers: The sunnah prayers before and after the obligatory prayers, Witr and Duha

questions.title: Questions
questions._comment: Each question pairs with the answer under it. 'More', 'Hijri date', 'Account', 'Your data', 'Export my data', 'Import from a file' and 'Send a diagnostic report' are screen names in the app: use the app's own wording in your language.
questions.timesQ: Why doesn’t the app show prayer times?
questions.timesA: On purpose. It tells you which part of the day you are in, and you tell it when you have prayed. A window that is three minutes out is invisible; a clock that is three minutes out contradicts your mosque.
questions.hijriQ: The Hijri date disagrees with my mosque.
questions.hijriA: Go to More, then Hijri date, and shift it by up to two days. Dates in the app are calculated, and calculation and local sighting often differ.
questions.expectedQ: Why does it say “expected” next to fasting days?
questions.expectedA: Because they are calculated, not sighted. Where readings differ, such as the ninth of Dhul Hijjah locally and the day of standing in Makkah, the app shows both rather than choosing for you.
questions.locationQ: I don’t want to share my location.
questions.locationA: You never have to. Pick your city instead, and everything works.
questions.notificationsA: Two or three a day by default, and none for the obligatory prayers unless you ask. You almost certainly have an adhan app already.
questions.computerQ: Does it work on my computer?
questions.computerA: Yes. The web app at {companionHost} runs in any modern browser, works offline and can be installed from your browser. A Chrome extension is coming soon to the Chrome Web Store.
questions.devicesQ: Can I use it on more than one device?
questions.devicesA: Yes. Sign in with Apple or Google under More, then Account, and your record syncs between your devices. Or, without an account, go to More, then Your data, then Export my data, and use Import from a file on the other device.
questions.brokenA: Go to More, then Your data, then Send a diagnostic report. It shows you everything it contains before anything is sent, and you choose where it goes. Or write to support@ihsaanly.app.

privacy._comment: The privacy policy. A legal text: translate faithfully rather than freely. <em> marks a path through the app's screens (shown unbroken, not italic): use the app's own screen names in your language. Rewritten 2026-09-29 for optional sign-in and sync.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.description: What Ihsaanly keeps on your device, what syncs if you choose to sign in, and your rights over it.
privacy.meta: Ihsaanly is published by Mohd Inc. Last updated {date}.
privacy.meta_comment: {date} is filled in by the build in this language's own date format.
privacy.summaryDevice: You do not need an account. Without signing in, your prayers, your settings and your practice are recorded on your device and stay there. There is no server involved and no analytics. The only optional exceptions, on iOS and Android, are announcements and crash reports: both are off until you turn them on, and neither includes your practice.
privacy.summarySync: If you choose to sign in with Apple or Google, your record is kept in your account so it syncs across your devices. It is never sold, never used for advertising, and you can delete it at any time.
privacy.summaryFeedback: If you are signed in, you can send us feedback from the app. We keep what you send, with your account identifier, so we can fix problems and improve the app.
privacy.scopeText: This policy covers the Ihsaanly app for iOS and Android, the web app at companion.ihsaanly.app, the Ihsaanly extension for Chrome, and this website. They are published by Mohd Inc. (“we”, “us”), which is responsible for your personal information.
privacy.storedTitle: What is stored on your device
privacy.storedMarks: Which prayers you have marked, and when
privacy.storedCompleted: Which optional acts you have completed
privacy.storedOwed: What you owe in make-up prayers and fasts
privacy.storedDay: Which items you have put on your day, and which you have marked as known
privacy.storedSuggested: Which optional act was last suggested to you, so you are not asked twice in a week
privacy.storedTravel: Whether you are travelling, and whether prayer tracking is paused
privacy.storedGender: Whether you chose Brother, Sister or preferred not to say when you set the app up. This decides only whether the app offers to pause prayer tracking, and it is used for nothing else
privacy.storedSettings: Your settings: location, calculation method, Hijri offset, reminders, language and appearance
privacy.storedHome: If you turn on leaving-home reminders, the coordinates of the one place you set as home
privacy.storedWhere: On iOS and Android all of it lives in a database on your device; in the web app and the extension, in your browser’s storage. Without an account it stays there, and we cannot see any of it.
privacy.contentUpdates: The app checks ihsaanly.app for updated content (sunnah items and their translations). This request sends nothing about you beyond what any web request includes (your IP address and your browser or app version), and nothing is logged by us beyond the host’s standard access logs.
privacy.locationRough: Ihsaanly needs a rough location to work out the parts of the day. You can grant location access, or pick a city from a list built into the app. The app works fully either way, and it works with no permissions granted at all.
privacy.locationNever: Your coordinates are used on your device to calculate prayer windows and the Hijri date. Without an account, they are never transmitted, except in a diagnostic report you choose to send (see below). If you sign in, your account keeps only a rounded location, accurate to about 1 km, with its city name and time zone, so your other devices use the same place.
privacy.locationGeofence: If you turn on leaving-home reminders, the app monitors a single region around a place you set. This is off by default and uses the device’s own geofencing. Your home location stays on the device: it is never sent anywhere, and it is not synced to your account.
privacy.syncIntro: Signing in is optional. It exists so your record follows you across your devices. You can sign in with Apple or Google (in the Chrome extension, with Google only). If you do, your account holds:
privacy.syncIdentity: Your email address and name, as Apple or Google share them. Apple may give a private relay address instead of your own
privacy.syncRecord: Your practice record: the prayers you have marked, the optional acts you have completed, what you owe in make-up prayers and fasts, and your fasting
privacy.syncProgress: Your progress: the items on your day and the items you have marked as known
privacy.syncSettings: Your settings: your location rounded to about 1 km, with its city name and time zone; your calculation method, Hijri offset, reminders, language and appearance; the choice you made when you set the app up; and whether you are travelling or prayer tracking is paused
privacy.syncNot: Your home location for leaving-home reminders stays on the device and is never synced. The app’s error log is never synced either, and leaves the device only if you turn on crash reports (see “Crash reports (optional)”).
privacy.processorsText: Sign-in is provided through Google Firebase Authentication, with Sign in with Apple or Google Sign-In. Your synced data is stored in Google Cloud Firestore, in Google’s United States multi-region (nam5). Google LLC processes it on our behalf as our service provider. Apple and Google also provide their own sign-in services independently, under their own privacy policies.
privacy.processorsTransfer: This means your synced data is stored in the United States. Where the law requires a safeguard for that transfer, as it does for people in the European Union and the United Kingdom, we rely on Google’s Standard Contractual Clauses and its certification under the EU–US Data Privacy Framework.
privacy.processorsSecurity: Your data is encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest by Google. Security rules allow only your own signed-in account to read or change it. We do not look at it, except where needed to operate the service, when you ask us to for support, or where the law requires it.
privacy.basesIntro: Where data protection laws such as the GDPR and the UK GDPR apply, we rely on these legal bases:
privacy.basesContract: Contract. We process your account data to provide the sync you asked for when you signed in.
privacy.basesConsent: Explicit consent. Your practice record reveals your religious practice (see below). You give your explicit consent to our processing it when you sign in, and you can withdraw that consent at any time.
privacy.basesInterests: Legitimate interests. We process the minimum needed to keep the service and your account secure.
privacy.basesFeedback: Legitimate interests and consent. We process the feedback you send to fix problems and improve the app (legitimate interests), and its optional diagnostic summary only if you turn it on (consent).
privacy.basesDevice: Without an account, we receive nothing, unless you send us a diagnostic report or an export yourself, or turn on crash reports.
privacy.sensitiveText: Your practice record reveals your religious practice, and whether prayer tracking is paused can relate to your health. Laws such as the GDPR treat these as special categories of data. We process them only with your explicit consent, given when you sign in, and only to provide the service to you.
privacy.leaveTitle: What else can leave your device, and only when you choose it
privacy.leaveTwo: Two things, both from More → Your data in the iOS and Android app and in the web app. Both are shared the way you choose, through your device’s share sheet or as a file you save, so you pick where they go.
privacy.leaveExport: Export my data. Your settings and your full practice record, as readable text, so you can keep it or move to a new device.
privacy.leaveReport: Send a diagnostic report. For fixing a problem. It contains your settings, your practice record, your approximate coordinates, your device and OS version, and any recent errors. Before anything is sent you are shown a screen listing exactly what it holds, and you can read the whole report in full. Coordinates in the report are rounded to about a hundred metres. Nothing is sent until you choose to send it, and you choose where it goes.
privacy.leaveReceive: We receive a diagnostic report or an export only if you choose to send it to us.
privacy.leaveFeedback: Send feedback. If you are signed in, you can send us a message from the app. It reaches us only when you tap Send (see “Feedback you send”).
privacy.feedbackIntro: People who are signed in can send feedback from the app. Nothing is sent until you tap Send. We store it in Google Cloud Firestore in the United States, linked to your account. It holds:
privacy.feedbackMessage: Your message, and its kind: a problem, an idea or other
privacy.feedbackContact: An optional contact email address, prefilled from your account, which you can change or remove
privacy.feedbackApp: Basic app and device information: where you are using Ihsaanly (iOS, Android, web or extension), the app version, the operating system and the language
privacy.feedbackDiagnostics: Only if you turn it on: a diagnostic summary with your app and device details, time zone, approximate location (about 1 km), recent error messages, notification settings and permission, and counts of the items you have recorded. It never includes your full practice record
privacy.feedbackPurpose: We use feedback only to fix problems and improve the app. Our legal bases are our legitimate interests, and your consent for the optional diagnostic summary, which you can leave off.
privacy.feedbackAccess: Once sent, you cannot read or change your feedback in the app. Only Mohd Inc. can read it.
privacy.feedbackRetention: We keep feedback for up to 2 years. Deleting your account does not erase it. We also keep a timestamp of the last feedback you sent, with it. To have it removed, email support@ihsaanly.app from the address linked to your account.
privacy.announcementsIntro: In the iOS and Android app, the Announcements switch lets us send you occasional announcements as push notifications. It is off by default, and nothing below happens until you turn it on. It is not available in the web app or the Chrome extension.
privacy.announcementsSent: What it does: when you turn it on, the app asks your device for permission to show notifications, then subscribes your device to two topics, “announcements” and “announcements-” followed by your app language, through Google Firebase Cloud Messaging.
privacy.announcementsToken: What delivers the messages: a device token that Google Firebase Cloud Messaging assigns to your installation (with a Firebase installation identifier) and, on iOS, the device token of Apple’s Push Notification service. Google and Apple hold these tokens to deliver the messages. We do not link them to your account, your practice or your settings, and we send announcements to a topic, not to individual people.
privacy.announcementsProcessors: Who processes it: Google (Firebase Cloud Messaging), which acts on our behalf as our service provider and may process this in the United States under the safeguards described above, and on iOS also Apple (Apple Push Notification service), under its own privacy policy.
privacy.announcementsBasis: Our legal basis is your consent, which you give by turning the switch on and allowing notifications. You can withdraw it at any time.
privacy.announcementsRetention: How long: your subscriptions last until you turn the switch off, or until the token expires because the app has not been used for a long time. Turning the switch off unsubscribes your device from the topics. Google keeps Firebase installation identifiers until they are deleted, and after deletion removes them from its live and backup systems within 180 days.
privacy.announcementsOff: How to turn it off: switch off Announcements in the app, or turn off notifications for Ihsaanly in your device’s settings.
privacy.crashIntro: In the iOS and Android app, the Share crash reports switch lets the app send us a report when it crashes or logs an error. It is off by default: until you turn it on, no crash data is collected or sent. It is not available in the web app or the Chrome extension. When it is on, these are sent through Google Firebase Crashlytics:
privacy.crashReports: The details of a crash: a stack trace and the state of the app when it happened
privacy.crashLog: Entries from the app’s error log
privacy.crashDevice: Your device model, operating system and app version
privacy.crashId: A Firebase installation identifier and a crash identifier, so reports can be grouped and the number of devices affected by a problem can be counted
privacy.crashNever: Reports are not linked to your account: we never attach a user identifier, and they never include your practice record, your settings or your account details.
privacy.crashProcessors: Who processes it: Google (Firebase Crashlytics), which processes reports on our behalf as our service provider, in the United States under the safeguards described above.
privacy.crashBasis: Our legal basis is your consent, which you give by turning the switch on. You can withdraw it at any time.
privacy.crashRetention: How long: Google keeps crash stack traces and their associated identifiers (including the Firebase installation identifier) for 90 days, then begins removing them from its live and backup systems.
privacy.crashOff: How to turn it off: switch off Share crash reports in the app. New reports stop at once; reports already sent are removed on the schedule above.
privacy.notAccount: No account required. Without signing in, the app never asks for an email address, a name or a phone number
privacy.notAds: No advertising, and no advertising identifier
privacy.notAnalytics: No analytics or telemetry, no advertising identifier and no Firebase Analytics. Crash reports and announcements are optional, off until you turn them on, and described above
privacy.notTracking: No tracking across apps or websites
privacy.notSelling: No selling or sharing of your personal information, and no use of it for advertising
privacy.retentionText: Data on your device stays until you delete it or remove the app. Your account and its synced data are kept until you delete your account.
privacy.retentionDelete: Deleting your account erases its cloud copy of your data immediately, and then the account itself. Any remaining copies in Google’s systems are removed on Google’s standard deletion schedule.
privacy.retentionFeedback: Feedback you send is kept for up to 2 years and is not erased when you delete your account. Email us to have it removed.
privacy.retentionSignOut: Signing out stops syncing on that device and asks whether to keep or remove the copy on it. Uninstalling the app or clearing your browser does not delete your account or its cloud copy: to remove those, delete your account.
privacy.rightsIntro: Depending on where you live, laws such as the GDPR, the UK GDPR, the California Consumer Privacy Act (as amended by the CPRA) and Canada’s PIPEDA give you rights over your personal information. We offer these to everyone:
privacy.rightsAccess: Access and portability. Use More → Your data → Export my data, or email us for a copy of what your account holds.
privacy.rightsRectify: Correction. Change anything in the app and the change syncs, or email us.
privacy.rightsErase: Erasure. Delete your account in the app, or by email. Deleting your account explains both.
privacy.rightsFeedback: Feedback. Deleting your account does not erase feedback you sent. Email us to access, correct or remove it.
privacy.rightsRestrict: Restriction and objection. Email us to restrict or object to how we process your data.
privacy.rightsWithdraw: Withdrawing consent. Sign out and delete your account, at any time. The app goes on working fully without an account.
privacy.rightsComplain: Complaints. You can complain to a data protection supervisory authority in the European Union or the United Kingdom, or to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada.
privacy.rightsHow: To use any of these rights, email support@ihsaanly.app from the address linked to your account, so we can confirm the request is yours.
privacy.californiaCollected: From people who sign in, we collect these categories of personal information: identifiers (email address, name and an account identifier); approximate geolocation (rounded to about 1 km); and sensitive personal information, namely religious beliefs as they can be inferred from your practice record. From people who neither sign in nor turn on crash reports, we collect nothing. Crash reports, if you turn them on, are described under “Crash reports (optional)”; they are not linked to your account.
privacy.californiaPurpose: We use this information only to provide your account and sync, and to keep the service secure. We disclose it only to our service provider, Google, which stores it for us. We use sensitive personal information only to provide the service you asked for.
privacy.californiaNoSale: We do not sell or share personal information, as the CCPA defines those words, and we will not treat you differently for using your privacy rights.
privacy.childrenText: Ihsaanly is not directed at children under 13. Signing in is for people aged 13 or older, or older where your country sets a higher age for consenting to online services yourself (up to 16). If you believe a child has an account, email us and we will delete it. Without an account and with crash reports off, the app collects nothing from anyone, of any age.
privacy.siteText: This website sets no cookies, runs no analytics and loads nothing from any other company. Like any web server, the host may keep standard access logs, such as your IP address and the page requested, for security and operation.
privacy.siteStorage: If you choose a language or an appearance on this website, your browser remembers that choice on your own device (in local storage). It is never sent to us.
privacy.siteApp: The web app and the Chrome extension keep the app’s data in your browser’s local storage. If you sign in, Firebase keeps your sign-in session in your browser’s storage (IndexedDB).
privacy.siteNecessary: All of this is strictly necessary for what you have asked for, and nothing else is stored. That is why there is no cookie banner.
privacy.donationsFree: Ihsaanly is free. Every part of it is free, and stays free. There is no paid tier, nothing is locked, and there is no advertising.
privacy.donationsOptional: You may give an optional donation, which unlocks nothing and changes nothing about the app. Donations are made at donate.ihsaanly.app, outside the app, and handled by its payment processor. The Android app links there; the other versions do not show it. Whatever that page collects is covered by its own privacy policy, not this one, and we never see your payment details. For questions about a donation, including refunds, email support@ihsaanly.app.
privacy.deleteText: More → Your data → Delete my data removes everything on this device and starts the app over.
privacy.deleteAccountText: If you have signed in, More → Account → Delete account erases your account and everything synced to it. You can also ask us by email. Deleting your account explains both.
privacy.changesText: When this policy changes, we update the date at the top of this page. Where the law requires your consent to a change, we will ask for it.
privacy.contactText: Mohd Inc. is the controller of your personal information. For any privacy question or request, write to us:

terms.religiousGuide: The app presents recommended acts with their sources: the verse, or the hadith collection with its reference and grading. terms.accountsText: You can use the app without an account. If you choose to sign in with Apple or Google, your record syncs across your devices. terms.accountsEnd: You can delete your account at any time, in the app or by email. We may suspend or close an account that abuses the service, or where the law requires us to.
terms.dataText: Without an account, everything the app records stays on your device. deleteAccount._comment: How to delete an Ihsaanly account. Google Play requires this page. A legal text: translate faithfully. <em> marks a path through the app's screens: use the app's own screen names in your language.
deleteAccount.title: Deleting your account
deleteAccount.description: How to delete your Ihsaanly account and the data synced to it, in the app or by email.
deleteAccount.meta: Ihsaanly is published by Mohd Inc. Last updated {date}.
deleteAccount.summaryApp: You can delete your Ihsaanly account yourself, at any time, from inside the app.
deleteAccount.summaryEmail: If you can no longer use the app, email us and we will delete it for you.
deleteAccount.noAccount: If you never signed in, there is no account to delete: everything is on your device, and More → Your data → Delete my data removes it.
deleteAccount.appIntro: The steps are the same in the iOS and Android app, the web app at companion.ihsaanly.app and the Chrome extension:
deleteAccount.appStep1: Sign in with the account you want to delete, if you are not signed in already.
deleteAccount.appStep4: Choose whether to keep the data on that device, to go on using the app without an account, or to remove it.
deleteAccount.appAfter: Your cloud copy is erased immediately, and then the account itself.
deleteAccount.emailText: Email support@ihsaanly.app from the email address of your account, with the subject “Delete my account”. We verify that the request comes from the account’s owner, delete the account within 30 days, and confirm by email when it is done.
deleteAccount.deletedRecord: Your practice record and progress stored in the cloud
deleteAccount.deletedSettings: Your settings stored in the cloud, including your approximate location
deleteAccount.deletedAccount: Your account itself: your email address, name and account identifier
deleteAccount.deletedBackups: Any remaining copies in Google’s systems are removed on Google’s standard deletion schedule.
deleteAccount.keptDevices: Data on devices you keep. Remove it from each one with More → Your data → Delete my data, or by choosing to remove it when you delete the account or sign out.
deleteAccount.keptFeedback: Feedback you sent from the app. It is kept for up to 2 years and is not erased with your account. To have it removed, email support@ihsaanly.app from the address linked to your account, with the subject “Remove my feedback”.
deleteAccount.keptDonations: Records of any donation, which are held by the donation processor at donate.ihsaanly.app, not by the app.
deleteAccount.privacyLink: The privacy policy explains what your account holds and how long it is kept.
